The body shall attain strength and become free from all ailments. By this method, truly, the lord of yogis becomes free from all disturbances on this earthly sphere. 56

### Now, Shitali

The wise practitioner should draw in the air with the tongue and practice retention <term>kumbhaka</term> <gloss>breath-holding</gloss> as described before. Then, they should slowly exhale the air through both nostrils. 57

This breath retention called <term>shitali</term> <gloss>the cooling breath</gloss> surely destroys diseases such as enlargement of the glands and spleen, as well as fever, bile disorders, hunger, thirst, and the effects of poisons. 58

---

-> Commentary <-

Regarding the verse beginning with "The body": Strength and power of the body shall manifest. By this stated method of practice, the lord of yogis—one who is like a King among yogis—shall truly be free from all obstacles and calamities on the earthly plane. Following the logical principle that "every statement carries an emphasis," the results described here are indeed true. 56

The author describes the <term>shitali kumbhaka</term> <gloss>cooling breath retention</gloss>: He says "with the tongue." This means drawing in the air by extending the tongue slightly beyond the lips, shaped like the lower beak of a bird, and performing a slow inhalation <term>puraka</term>. Then, one should perform the practice of retention <term>kumbhaka</term> as previously described for the <term>suryabhedana</term> <gloss>sun-piercing breath</gloss> practice. The wise practitioner—one possessed of a refined intellect—should then exhale the air slowly through the two openings of the nostrils. 57

The benefits of <term>shitali</term> are described: Diseases such as <term>gulma</term> <gloss>chronic enlargement of the abdominal glands</gloss> and <term>pliha</term> <gloss>splenic disorders</gloss>, as well as fever, disorders caused by excess <term>pitta</term> <gloss>the fire/bile humor</gloss>, hunger <note>the desire to eat</note>, thirst <note>the desire to drink water</note>, and the complications arising from the poisons of snakes and other sources. This well-known practice called <term>shitali</term> completely destroys these afflictions. The word <term>kumbhika</term> <gloss>small pot/retention</gloss> is used in the feminine... 58

---

-> Vernacular Language Translation <-

Regarding "The body": The body gains strength. By following this method of practice, a person becomes like an Indra <note>the King of Gods</note> among yogis on this earth and remains free from all disturbances. The fruit of the practice described here is truth. 56

Now the fourth breath retention, <term>shitali</term>, is described: "With the tongue." One should extend the tongue outside the lips like the lower beak of a bird and pull the air inward to fill the lungs. Then, perform retention just as described earlier for <term>suryabhedana</term>. Afterward, the practitioner of beautiful intellect should slowly exhale the air through the holes of the nose. 57

The qualities of <term>shitali</term> are described: Diseases beginning with <term>gulma</term> and <term>pliha</term>, fever, disorders of the <term>pitta</term> humor, the desire for food, the desire for water, the venom from snake bites, and other poisons are all removed by this <term>kumbhika</term> called <term>shitali</term>. 58

<summary>This page describes the technique and benefits of Shitali Kumbhaka, a cooling breathing practice where air is inhaled through a rolled tongue. It is cited as a cure for fever, thirst, hunger, and various internal ailments including the effects of poison.</summary>
